state_sync.interpretation: The old 25-unit alarm is historical. This addendum searches for independent formulations, generalizations, barriers, and discovery-complexity results without changing JANUS runtime.

new_missed_lanes.finding: The N58 dangerous regime is naturally a two-codebook, almost-separable zero-error decoding problem for a coordinatewise symmetric partial channel: P and Q are codebooks over {OMIT,POS,NEG}; compatible pairs emit the signed union, while any POS/NEG clash is rejected as tautological. A historical J>=610 of pq=616 means at most six pair-edges fail to have mutually unique new outputs.

closest_primary_sources.title: Separable Codes for the Symmetric Multiple-Access Channel
closest_primary_sources.result: Defines separable codes for arbitrary noiseless symmetric coordinatewise MACs and explicitly defines almost separable codes by the fraction of bad messages; gives combinatorial and entropy rate bounds.

closest_primary_sources.title: Coding for a Multiple-Access Channel
closest_primary_sources.result: Defines unique decodability for a two-codebook binary erasure MAC through a symmetric coordinate map E(u,v), providing an exact code-pair precedent.

new_missed_lanes.why_close: Unlike ordinary cancellative-set theory, this literature natively speaks about deterministic coordinatewise outputs, codeword pairs, collisions, and almost-unique decoding.
new_missed_lanes.why_not_direct: Published theorems use one shared codebook or a different channel alphabet/function. JANUS also discards tautological pairs instead of assigning them an ordinary output. A bipartite code-pair theorem for the exact JANUS partial channel has not been located.

new_missed_lanes.finding: K-union-distinct families require every union of at most K members to be distinct; superimposed/separable codes encode the same Boolean-OR uniqueness problem. This is a closer operation-level match than additive Sidon systems.

closest_primary_sources.title: Union Distinct Families of Sets, with an Application to Cryptography
closest_primary_sources.result: Defines K-union-distinct families; shows cover-free is sufficient but not necessary and constructs union-distinct families via partially cover-free structure.

closest_primary_sources.title: Some new results on superimposed codes
closest_primary_sources.result: Studies cover-free/superimposed-code structures and exact small parameter cases.

new_missed_lanes.why_close: The JANUS B12 literal encoding turns a signed compatible union into ordinary set union on partial transversals.
new_missed_lanes.why_not_direct: Standard union-distinct families use one family and all pair unions; JANUS is bipartite P x Q, partial compatibility, retained-clause exclusions, and incidence constraints.

new_missed_lanes.finding: Two-family multiset-union-free pairs are exactly uniquely decodable two-codebook systems under coordinatewise integer addition. The literature provides soft Sauer-Perles-Shelah and entropy methods that may be adaptable to JANUS omission/sign marginals.

closest_primary_sources.title: An Upper Bound on the Sizes of Multiset-Union-Free Families
closest_primary_sources.result: For two families F1,F2 requires A⊎C=B⊎D only for the identical parent pair; derives zero-error capacity-region upper bounds using a soft Sauer-Perles-Shelah lemma and information-theoretic inequalities.

new_missed_lanes.why_close: Two independent parent families are part of the theorem statement, and coordinate marginals drive the upper bound.
new_missed_lanes.why_not_direct: Multiset union remembers multiplicity while a JANUS resolvent union does not; their main bounds are asymptotic and ordinary binary-set based. Equality of multiset unions implies equality of set unions, not conversely.

new_missed_lanes.finding: The historical N58 regime is near-injective rather than exactly cancellative, so weak union-free, 2-cancellative, and almost-cancellative formulations are better conceptual matches than exact cancellative pairs.

closest_primary_sources.title: New Bounds for Union-free Families of Sets
closest_primary_sources.result: Studies weakly union-free and strongly union-free families, separating four-distinct-set union collisions from stronger cancellativity.

closest_primary_sources.title: 2-Cancellative Hypergraphs and Codes
closest_primary_sources.result: Studies t-cancellative union collision restrictions and asymptotic upper bounds.

excluded_navigation_only.title: Asymptotics of the maximal size of almost cancellative families of sets
excluded_navigation_only.author: Vladimir Balakirsky

new_missed_lanes.why_not_direct: Available published results are one-family, unsigned and primarily asymptotic; no finite bipartite signed theorem matching 22 x 28 on six coordinates was found.

new_missed_lanes.finding: Pair descendants record, per coordinate, the set of symbols appearing in the two parents. Distinct pair descendants are an established code-design problem with packing and graph-theoretic bounds.

closest_primary_sources.title: On Codes with the Identifiable Parent Property
New bounds on bar-2-separable codes of length 2
A note on bar-2-separable codes and B2 codes

new_missed_lanes.exact_relation: If two compatible JANUS pair-unions differ, their descendant signatures differ. The converse is false because descendants remember whether OMIT participated, so descendant separability is strictly stronger information than resolvent-union separability.

new_missed_lanes.finding: Near-extremal separability problems often become C4-free or short-cycle-free bipartite graph problems. Supersaturation results then force many collisions once a threshold is crossed.

closest_primary_sources.title: Supersaturation of C4: From Zarankiewicz towards Erdos-Simonovits-Sidorenko
closest_primary_sources.result: Gives exact C4 supersaturation/stability near the Zarankiewicz threshold.

new_missed_lanes.why_not_direct: No sound reduction has yet been proved from equality of JANUS signed unions to a C4 in a parent graph. Therefore C4 bounds cannot currently be inserted numerically.

new_missed_lanes.finding: There are CNF classes where a specially chosen DP variable has the property that every resolvent is contained in a parent, preventing clause explosion. This is qualitatively much stronger than generic pq counting.

closest_primary_sources.title: Satisfiability of acyclic and almost acyclic CNF formulas
closest_primary_sources.result: For beta-acyclic CNFs establishes an elimination route through DP-simplicial variables; the resolvents created at such a step are subsumed by parent structure, yielding polynomial-time satisfiability for the class.

new_missed_lanes.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Theorem-side reachability/structure test before elimination: determine whether any JANUS canonical reachable state satisfies an analogous local DP-simplicial condition.
new_missed_lanes.why_not_direct: No DP-simplicial or beta-acyclic property has been proved for the frozen N58 state or for all JANUS reachable canonical states. Post-elimination subsumption remains forbidden as a free pre-raw resource.

classical_primary_backfill.title: A Computing Procedure for Quantification Theory
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Introduces the Davis-Putnam elimination procedure: eliminate a variable by resolving opposite-polarity clauses and deleting the pivot-containing parents.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Propositional CNF; exact variable elimination by resolution.
classical_primary_backfill.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Historical semantic baseline for JANUS elimination.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Direct model lineage.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: No nontrivial p,q/support growth ceiling matching N58 is supplied.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Directional Resolution: The Davis-Putnam Procedure, Revisited
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Directional resolution complexity is controlled by an ordering-induced width/diversity parameter rather than by raw clause count alone.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Ordered propositional/constraint elimination under a fixed variable ordering.
classical_primary_backfill.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Compare theorem-side elimination state with induced-width style structure.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Strong structural analogue for elimination growth.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: JANUS selector/minimum-incidence dynamics are not automatically the directional-resolution ordering assumed by the theorem.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Bucket elimination: A unifying framework for reasoning
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Bucket-elimination time and space are bounded exponentially in the induced width of the chosen elimination ordering.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Graphical-model/constraint reasoning represented by bucketed functions and a fixed elimination order.
classical_primary_backfill.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Potential external ceiling route if JANUS reachable incidence graph admits a certified width bound.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Exact elimination-width literature requested by Algorithmist.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: Function/bucket sizes are not the JANUS raw-unit accounting model; no width certificate is currently frozen for N58.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Effective Preprocessing in SAT through Variable and Clause Elimination
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Develops bounded variable elimination and clause elimination as practical SAT preprocessing, accepting an elimination only under explicit size/growth criteria and combining it with subsumption techniques.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: SAT preprocessing is allowed to alter the formula while preserving satisfiability and uses practical simplification resources.
classical_primary_backfill.resource_required: Bounded variable elimination plus preprocessing simplifications.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Directly discusses resolvent growth at variable elimination.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: JANUS may not import its post-generation subsumption/self-subsumption or heuristic acceptance criterion as theorem-side free resources.

classical_primary_backfill.title: On the complexity of regular resolution and the Davis-Putnam procedure
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Constructs contradictory formulas exhibiting exponential lower bounds for regular-resolution proof trees / Davis-Putnam style elimination, including generation of exponentially many distinct clauses.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Specific hard formula families and the regular/DP proof models studied in the paper.
classical_primary_backfill.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Destruction/barrier control for any claim that generic elimination cannot blow up.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Direct warning against turning local N58 success into an unbounded theorem.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: A lower bound for Galil's DP/regular model is not automatically a JANUS lower bound without a simulation/reachability theorem.

classical_primary_backfill.title: The Efficiency of Resolution and Davis--Putnam Procedures
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Relates resolution proof size to proof-search procedures and analyzes Davis-Putnam/DPLL-style performance, including average-case bounds.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Resolution/DP proof-search models with the paper's formula distributions and search procedures.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Relevant to separating existence of proofs from search cost.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: Does not establish a JANUS-specific lower or upper bound absent exact simulation.

classical_primary_backfill.title: To guess or to think? Hybrid algorithms for SAT
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Analyzes hybrid SAT procedures trading conditioning/search against resolution/elimination, with complexity governed by structural width parameters.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Hybrid conditioning plus directional-resolution framework.
classical_primary_backfill.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Resource map for what elimination gains when extra branching is admitted.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Useful negative control for resource accounting.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: JANUS cannot be credited with conditioning/search resources it does not possess.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Satisfiability of acyclic and almost acyclic CNF formulas
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Beta-acyclic CNFs admit elimination through DP-simplicial variables; the local resolvent structure prevents the generic combinatorial explosion and yields polynomial-time satisfiability for the class.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: CNFs in the beta-acyclic / DP-simplicial classes defined in the paper.
classical_primary_backfill.resource_required: Certified structural property of the incidence hypergraph / pivot.
classical_primary_backfill.candidate_janus_insertion_point: Reachability-side structural gate before JANUS elimination.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Potentially very strong exact local growth collapse if its premise can be independently proved.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: No beta-acyclic or DP-simplicial premise is currently established for N58/JANUS generally.

classical_primary_backfill.title: On Davis–Putnam reductions for minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: For minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets, singular DP-reduction preserves minimal unsatisfiability and deficiency and has confluence properties under additional saturation hypotheses.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Minimally unsatisfiable CNFs; singular pivot occurrence and, for stronger conclusions, saturation/eventual saturation.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Shows exact structural information can sharply constrain DP reductions.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: JANUS canonical state is not automatically minimally unsatisfiable, singular, or saturated.

classical_primary_backfill.title: On the automatizability of resolution and related propositional proof systems
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Defines weak automatizability; characterizes it via a weak satisfiability problem and proves equivalences linking weak automatizability of Resolution, Res(k), and feasible interpolation.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Standard propositional proof systems and polynomial dependence on smallest proof size.
classical_primary_backfill.resource_required: Proof-search algorithm relative to proof length; possibly stronger output system for weak automatability.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Directly separates proof-system existence from efficient proof discovery.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: No direct conclusion for JANUS without identifying the exact proof system and simulation.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Resolution Is Not Automatizable Unless W[P] Is Tractable
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Neither Resolution nor tree-like Resolution is automatizable unless W[P] is fixed-parameter tractable by randomized algorithms with one-sided error.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Automatability defined relative to shortest proofs; standard Resolution/tree-like Resolution.
classical_primary_backfill.resource_required: Hypothetical proof-search algorithm polynomial in input and shortest proof size.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Canonical source for SHORT_PROOF_EXISTS != CHEAP_DISCOVERY.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: Cannot be labeled a JANUS lower bound without a JANUS-to-Resolution simulation relation and matching complexity measure.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Complexity of finding short resolution proofs
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Studies computational hardness of finding short Resolution proofs rather than only existence/length of such proofs.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Resolution proof-search problem and the approximation/search regime defined in the paper.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Directly addresses the search-vs-existence distinction requested by Algorithmist.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: Exact quantitative hardness statement must not be transferred to JANUS without model equivalence.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Minimum propositional proof length is NP-hard to linearly approximate
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Determining minimum proof length is NP-hard to approximate within any constant factor for a broad range of proof systems including Resolution, with results applying to tree-like and DAG-like measures.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Natural propositional proof systems and proof length measured by symbols or inferences.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Strong evidence that short-proof length itself can be hard to infer.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: Approximation hardness for generic Resolution is not a JANUS runtime lower bound.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Automating Regular or Ordered Resolution is NP-Hard
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Regular and ordered (Davis-Putnam) Resolution are automatable iff P=NP; distinguishing polynomial ordered refutations from instances requiring exponential general-Resolution proofs is NP-complete.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Regular/ordered Resolution under the report's automatability formulation.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Especially relevant because ordered Resolution is explicitly Davis-Putnam style.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: Still a different proof-search model; no automatic transfer to JANUS.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Automating Tree-Like Resolution in Time n^{o(log n)} Is ETH-Hard
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Tree-like Resolution is not automatable in time n^{o(log n)} unless ETH fails, making the known quasipolynomial automation essentially optimal under ETH.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Tree-like Resolution and ETH.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Sharp conditional discovery lower bound.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: JANUS is not assumed tree-like Resolution.

classical_primary_backfill.title: On the Automatability of Tree-Like k-DNF Resolution
classical_primary_backfill.theorem_statement: Establishes conditional lower bounds for automating tree-like k-DNF Resolution.
classical_primary_backfill.exact_model_assumptions: Tree-like k-DNF Resolution under the paper's complexity assumptions.
classical_primary_backfill.resource_required: Proof-search in a stronger neighboring system.
classical_primary_backfill.applicability: Useful to prevent casual transfer from stronger proof syntax to easy discovery.
classical_primary_backfill.non_applicability: No JANUS simulation theorem; system contains k-DNF proof resources not credited to JANUS.

classical_primary_backfill.title: Regular resolution effectively simulates resolution

priority_red_handoff_summary: NEW BEST LANGUAGE: N58 historical near-injective state is naturally a BIPARTITE ALMOST-SEPARABLE CODE PAIR for a PARTIAL SYMMETRIC MAC.
NEW EXACT OPERATION LANE: K-union-distinct / superimposed codes study uniqueness of unions directly, not merely set intersections.
NEW TWO-FAMILY LANE: multiset-union-free code pairs provide entropy and soft-shattering methods with P and Q explicit.
NEW STRUCTURAL SAT LANE: DP-simplicial / beta-acyclic CNFs show that a certified local incidence-hypergraph property can collapse resolvent growth, but the premise is not proved for JANUS.
NO NEW DIRECT EXTERNAL INEQUALITY currently matches all JANUS assumptions and improves the already-closed N58 bound numerically.
120 DISTINCT PRIMARY CANDIDATE COVERAGE is now reachable after deduplication, but 120 full theorem/proof reviews are NOT claimed.
